mainTopic: The opening of the גמרא on the משנה about the כהן גדול's טבילות on יום הכיפורים: the name of לשכת בית הפרוה, the linen sheet, and the value of his morning and afternoon garments.
overview: The גמרא explains several details of the משנה about the כהן גדול's immersions on יום הכיפורים. First, רב יוסף says that פרוה, the name of the chamber, was a Persian sorcerer. Next, רב כהנא explains why the sheet spread around the כהן גדול was made of בוץ (fine linen). It reminds him that the special service of the day is done in linen garments. The גמרא then asks why the משנה adds up the value of the morning and afternoon garments. It answers that the total is a minimum, and the value may be shifted between the two sets as long as the total is kept. Finally, the גמרא notes that all opinions agree the morning garments must be the finer ones. רב הונא בריה דרב עילאי learns this from the four times ״בד״ appears in the פסוק, which teaches that the choicest linen is required.

steps.title: Who or what is פרוה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the name ״פרוה״ in the משנה means.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about a name the משנה mentioned, the chamber called בית הפרוה. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the טבילה took place on the roof of בית הפרוה. It never explained the name. The גמרא asks for its meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
The name of a chamber in the עזרה

phrases.notes: Refers to the chamber called בית הפרוה in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning or origin of the name פרוה.

steps.title: פרוה was a Persian sorcerer
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that פרוה was the name of a Persian sorcerer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: פרוה was a sorcerer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question. פרוה was a person, a Persian sorcerer (an אמגושא), and the chamber was named after him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chamber's name is not a description of the room itself. It is named after a person connected to it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרוה was a Persian sorcerer, and the chamber is named after him.

steps.title: Why was the sheet made of fine linen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about a בוץ sheet and asks why it had to be linen specifically.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] They spread a sheet of fine linen. What is different that it is of fine linen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks why the sheet had to be בוץ. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sheet was only there as a screen while the כהן גדול undressed and immersed. Any material should work for that. So why does the משנה specify fine linen?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this specifically?

phrases.english: They spread a sheet of fine linen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next detail of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the screen sheet had to be made of linen.

steps.title: A reminder that the day's service is in linen
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that the linen sheet reminds the כהן גדול that the special service of יום הכיפורים is done in linen garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: So that he will recognize that the service of the day is in linen garments.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers that the linen sheet works as a reminder. Seeing linen tells the כהן גדול that today's special עבודה is done in בגדי לבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים the כהן גדול switches between the golden garments and the white linen garments. The linen sheet is a visual cue, so he keeps track that the unique עבודת היום belongs to linen.

keyTerms.meaning: That he will recognize or be aware
The special service of יום הכיפורים

phrases.english: So that he will be aware
That the service of the day is in linen garments.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The linen sheet reminds the כהן גדול that the day's service is performed in linen.

steps.title: Why does the משנה add up the total?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about garments worth 18 and 12 מנה and asks why the תנא bothers to give the total.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] In the morning he would wear Pelusium garments worth eighteen [מנה], etc. Did the תנא come to teach us arithmetic?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the value of the garments. It then challenges why the משנה adds them up ("all together thirty מנה"), since anyone can do the math.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states that the morning garments cost 18 מנה and the afternoon ones 12 מנה, and then adds "in total 30." A תנא does not teach simple addition. So the total must be teaching something else.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine garments made in Pelusium, Egypt

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether the numbers are correct. It asks why the משנה needs to state the sum at all, which suggests the sum itself is a rule.

phrases.english: In the morning he would wear
Did the tanna come to teach us a tally?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement of the total ("הכל שלשים מנה").
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stating a sum the reader can compute seems pointless, so it must carry a legal meaning.

steps.title: The total is a minimum
steps.stepSummary: The total teaches that the garments together may not be made for less than that amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that we may not make them for less than these.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the total sets a minimum. The combined cost of both sets of garments may not be lower than the total.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sum is not arithmetic. It is a rule: the overall value cannot drop below the stated figure.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

phrases.english: That we do not make [them] for less than these.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording: the total is a legal minimum.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sum looked like useless arithmetic.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sum sets a minimum combined value for the garments.

steps.title: The total may be redistributed between the sets
steps.stepSummary: Since the total is what matters, one may lower the value of one set and raise the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if one reduced from these and added to those, we have no problem with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the practical result of the answer. As long as the total is kept, the money can be shifted between the morning and afternoon garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The individual figures in the משנה are not fixed. Only the combined minimum is required, so moving value from one set to the other is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: We have no problem with it

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's total is a minimum combined value, not a fixed price for each set. The split between the morning and afternoon garments is flexible.

phrases.english: But if one reduced from these
We have no problem with it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אִי בָּצֵיר מֵהָנֵי וְטָפֵי אַהֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the practical result of the answer in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only the total minimum is required. Value may be shifted between the two sets of garments.

steps.title: Source that the morning garments must be finer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that everyone agrees the morning garments must be the more valuable ones, and it asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, according to everyone, the morning [garments] are superior. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that both רבי מאיר and חכמים agree the morning garments must be worth more. It asks where this is learned, and the next step gives the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two opinions in the משנה give different numbers, but in both the morning set costs more. So there is a shared rule that the morning garments are superior. That rule limits the flexibility allowed in step 7, and it needs a source.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 7 allows shifting value between the sets. That shift may not go so far that the afternoon garments become finer than the morning ones.

phrases.english: In any case, according to everyone,
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא מִיהַת דְּשַׁחַר עֲדִיפִי מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Notes a point of agreement within the משנה's dispute and seeks its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the morning garments must be more valuable.

steps.title: Four times linen means the choicest linen
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב עילאי learns from the four mentions of ״בד״ in the פסוק that the choicest linen is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב עילאי said: The verse says "linen," "linen," "linen," "linen" — the choicest of linen.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב עילאי answers from the פסוק in ויקרא טז:ד, which repeats ״בד״ four times about the morning garments. From this he learns that they must be of the best linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said "linen" once. The repetition is extra, and it teaches that the garments must be the finest linen. That is why the morning garments must be more valuable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the halacha that the morning garments of יום הכיפורים must be of superior quality. Any redistribution of value between the two sets must keep the morning set finer.
steps.whatToRemember: All agree the morning garments are finer, learned from the fourfold ״בד״, which means the choicest linen (מובחר בבד).

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב עִילָּאֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Ilai said:

phrases.notes: ויקרא טז:ד: the tunic, trousers, belt, and mitre.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fourfold repetition of ״בד״ teaches that the choicest linen is required, so the morning garments must be superior.
